work.note: The Golden Goose é um conto de fadas dos Irmãos Grimm sobre um rapaz bondoso que divide o seu lanche com um velhinho e ganha um ganso de penas de ouro. A referência é o conto em que ser educado leva à recompensa: please, thank you.

pages.title: Dinner and a thank-you · 1/3
paragraphs: I am in **Nashville**, the city of music. Tonight my friend Nora and I have dinner in a restaurant with live guitar. The food is great, and the server, Cole, is friendly.

After dinner, Cole asks, “**How was everything?**” I say, “**Great, thank you!**” He brings the check. “**Here’s your check.**” I look at it and ask, “**How much is the tip?**” He says, “**Fifteen to twenty percent.**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Dinner and a thank-you · 2/3
paragraphs: I think for a moment. The service was very good, and Cole worked hard. “**Okay. Twenty percent, then**,” I say. Cole smiles. “**You’re so kind. Thank you!**” “**Have a great night!**” I say. “**Have a lovely night!**” he answers.

Nora tells me about a fairy tale called The Golden Goose. In the story, a kind boy shares his cake with a little man, and he gets a golden prize. The story says kindness is a treasure. A tip is a small way to be kind, too.

pages.title: Dinner and a thank-you · 3/3
paragraphs: I leave the restaurant happy. Good food, good music and good manners: that is a perfect night. I know the important words: tip, change, percent and service. Don’t forget the tip!
